title: Brian Schottenheimer on Hottest Seat in NFL After Cowboys Fall to Buccaneers 24-16
text:
Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer now sits on the hottest seat in the NFL after a 24-16 home loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, a game that may have cooled Todd Bowles' job security instead.
Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer now sits on the hottest seat in the NFL after his team fell 24-16 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at AT&T Stadium on Thursday night.
Schottenheimer was stumped on the sideline as his squad collapsed in primetime. The loss dropped Dallas to a frustrating place as the season nears its midpoint. The reason Schottenheimer's seat is the hottest is because the man facing him on the opposite sideline came into Week 5 in that position first. Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles is fighting for his job security after a brutal start to the season.
Yes, his starting quarterback, Baker Mayfield, is out, but the Buccaneers did not look good before his injury. And since Tampa Bay couldn't make the playoffs last season despite a red-hot start, Bowles needs to start stacking wins. The state of Tampa Bay, and a Dallas victory over the Houston Texans in Week 4, led Vegas to mark the Cowboys as a clear-cut favorite at home.
But Dak Prescott never felt comfortable like he did in Week 4, with Bowles drawing up his signature blitzes throughout the four quarters, and the Dallas defense continued to be passive. Jalon Daniels was quite efficient against a reeling Cowboys defense, which came into this game as the third-worst in the league in terms of yards allowed per game (389.5) and fifth-worst in points allowed (28).
Dallas Defense Struggles Persist in 2026
The defensive side of the ball was a problem during Schottenheimer's inaugural season leading the Cowboys in 2025, and with 34-year-old Christian Parker as defensive coordinator, it's more of the same in 2026. Armando said, I just thought, you know, that's a good offense. That's a lot of good players. Yeah.
They're going to score a lot of points and they are. And I thought that their total rebranding of the defense was going to work. And it didn't last night. Tampa Bay found itself down at halftime, 10-7, but shifty running back Bucky Irving changed the entire momentum of the contest when he sprinted 72 yards on the opening drive of the third quarter to set up an Emeka Egbuka touchdown.
In just two plays, the Bucs went 86 yards and took the lead, shocking the sold-out crowd. To make matters worse, the Cowboys would turn the ball over their next three possessions, leading to a lopsided game. Prescott threw an interception, and Daniels found Tez Johnson in busted coverage for a 64-yard catch-and-run.
Cowboys Turnovers Lead to Lopsided Score
Irving scored his second touchdown of the game to further the Bucs' lead, and Prescott wouldn't even get the ball back after KaVontae Turpin fumbled the ensuing kickoff, which Tampa Bay recovered. With a Chase McLaughlin field goal making it 24-10, the Cowboys felt desperate at the end of the third quarter, going for it on fourth down near midfield and failing to convert. There was, however, some hope provided by a key stop from this lackluster defense.
On fourth-and-goal from the one-yard line, Bowles decided to go for the kill shot, hoping to punch one into the end zone and make it a 31-10 game in the fourth quarter. But Sean Tucker, their short-yardage specialist in the backfield, was unable to punch it home. From there, Schottenheimer put on his best play-calling hat and recognized that momentum was shifting toward Dallas despite the Buccaneers' 99-yard drive. He and Prescott delivered.
George Pickens capped that 99-yard drive with a 17-yard touchdown catch, his first of the season, to make it a one score game after a two-point conversion failed. The momentum continued, as the Buccaneers went three-and-out, and with ample time as well as timeouts, Prescott could go down the field and perhaps tie the game with a touchdown and two-point conversion.
Ferguson Drop Ends Cowboys Rally Hopes
Instead, more disaster for the Cowboys in this primetime matchup, as tight end Jake Ferguson, usually as sure-handed as they come for Dallas, had a Prescott pass go right through his hands, hit his face mask and land in the arms of Buccaneers linebacker Alex Anzalone while in Tampa Bay territory. This time, Daniels and the Buccaneers' offense didn't squander the chance to put the Cowboys away, as Irving picked up the necessary first down to allow his rookie quarterback some victory kneels to end the game.
Bucky Irving of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers celebrated after scoring a touchdown during the second quarter of the NFL game. The Cowboys' collapse leaves Schottenheimer facing intense scrutiny while Bowles finally has a win to build on.
